plain.li: The villages down the road have had hard years too. It's time we gave something back.
A tenth is small enough that we won't miss it and large enough that they'll notice.

warm.li: I'd like the villages to know our name for more than our walls.

blunt.li: We can afford it. So give it.

cheerful.li: Imagine the traders saying our name and smiling!

gloomy.li: One day we'll need friends. Better to make them while we can.

cold.li: Forty silver a day at most, to a neighbor who'll owe us for it. Reasonable.

plain.li: Give it away every morning, and one morning there won't be any to give.
I'd rather we chose who to help than hand a tenth over blind.

warm.li: I'd sooner give to the faces I know than send it off down the road.

cheerful.li: I was saving for a new coat! I suppose a tenth of a coat is still a sleeve.

cold.li: A tenth every day for nothing in hand. Show me the return.

plain.li: I want to know where everyone is after dark. A curfew tells me.
The night watch can do its job when nobody else is wandering about.

warm.li: Everyone safe in bed by ten. I'd sleep better knowing that.

blunt.li: Bed by ten. Bar the gate. Simple.

cheerful.li: An early night for everyone! We could all use one.

plain.li: The evening is the only time I have to myself.
Some of the work only gets done after dark, and now it won't.

warm.li: I'll miss sitting up with friends by the fire.

gloomy.li: Barred in at night like animals. Next it'll be the days.

cold.li: Seven hours a night for five nights. Thirty-five hours lost, for each of us.

plain.li: When the raiders come, I want everyone to have practiced at least once.
An hour of drill each evening, and we'll all sleep easier.

warm.li: I'd like everyone to be able to look after themselves, and each other.

gloomy.li: They'll come again. Better to meet them with practiced hands.

cold.li: A colony where everyone can fight is a poor target for raiders.

plain.li: An hour every evening adds up to a lot of hours.
My hoe and my spear want the same hours, and it's the hoe that feeds us.

blunt.li: I can fight already. Leave me out.

cheerful.li: Drills again? My aim's terrible and everyone knows it.

cold.li: Untrained people with weapons are a danger to their neighbors.

plain.li: A few sacks a day costs us less than the guilt of doing nothing.
They're hungry and we're not. That's the whole of the argument.

cheerful.li: Bread for the village! They'll remember us kindly for it.

gloomy.li: We were hungry once. We'll be hungry again. Feed them now.

plain.li: Every sack that goes out the gate is one we don't have in spring.
I'd help a neighbor I know. Sending food off to strangers is another thing.

warm.li: I want to help them. I just want our own children fed first.

cheerful.li: Alms are lovely until the stores are empty.

cold.li: Feed a village once and they'll count on it every winter after.

plain.li: We keep the work going every day of the year. Three days for the faith won't sink us.
People need something more than chores to hold them together.

blunt.li: Three days. Pray. Then back to work.

cheerful.li: Holy days! I've been looking forward to the songs.

gloomy.li: We've had a hard season. The faith is what got us through it.

plain.li: Three days of slow work, right when we can least afford it.
I'll pray in my own time. I don't need a decree for it.

warm.li: I respect the faith. I'd just rather not be made to keep it.

cheerful.li: Three days of prayers? I'll fall asleep in the second one.

cold.li: Faith that needs a decree to keep it isn't worth much.

plain.li: A market day would bring the neighbors to us, for once.
We need cloth and medicine, and we have more grain than we'll eat. Call a market.

warm.li: A market day brings people together. We could use the company.

blunt.li: We have goods. They have silver. Market.

gloomy.li: Trade while there's still someone to trade with.

plain.li: Two days of haggling and nothing much done.
Every market I've been to, I came home poorer.

warm.li: I'd rather trade quietly than open the gates to everyone.

cheerful.li: A market? I'll spend everything I have on something I don't need.

cold.li: Strangers walking our stores, noting what we have. I don't like it.

plain.li: Two days of bread and water, and the stores go further than you'd think.
A fast clears the head. I've done it before and I'll do it again.

cheerful.li: Fasting! I've heard it makes you sharper. I'll let you know.

gloomy.li: I've gone hungry for worse reasons than this.

plain.li: I can't haul stone on bread and water.
We work too hard to eat this little.

warm.li: The children and the sick shouldn't go hungry for a decree.

cold.li: A fast slows every pair of hands in the colony. That's a poor trade.

plain.li: A song keeps everyone pulling at the same time.
The hours go quicker when someone's singing.

blunt.li: Sing and work. Both at once. Easy.

gloomy.li: If we're going to work this hard, we might as well sing.

cold.li: Rhythm makes hauling efficient. The songs are a side effect.

plain.li: I can't hear myself think.
There's a time for singing. It's not while I'm counting.

warm.li: I love a song, just not every hour of every day.

cheerful.li: I like the singing. I just wish they knew more than one song.

gloomy.li: Same song, same field, same aching back.

plain.li: A lonely week is better than a fever through every bed in the place.
The sick get better faster when they're kept apart and quiet.

warm.li: It's to protect the little ones and the old. That's reason enough.

blunt.li: Close the gate. Keep apart. Live.

cheerful.li: A bit of distance for a while, then a big party when it's over.

plain.li: I'm not the one coughing. I don't see why I'm locked away.
The sick need company as much as rest.

cheerful.li: Quarantine? I'll go mad with only myself to talk to.

gloomy.li: Shut away from everyone. It's like being buried early.

cold.li: Turning away every visitor costs us more than the risk.

plain.li: We have bread and they have none. I couldn't eat mine knowing that.
Smaller bowls for a while. We'll manage, and so will they.

cheerful.li: A little hungrier and a lot better liked. I'll take that.

gloomy.li: When the famine's over, they'll remember who fed them, and who didn't.

plain.li: Famines spread. Ours could be next, with half our stores already given away.
I'll give what I can spare. I can't spare a share every morning.

warm.li: My heart says yes. My stomach and my children say no.

cheerful.li: I'll share, but I'm keeping the crusts.

cold.li: Our own stores are thin enough. Charity can wait for a better year.

plain.li: Some of the best people here came in off the road. There'll be more.
We've kept the gate shut long enough. Let's see who comes.

warm.li: A traveler should find a welcome here. That's the kind of place I want.

blunt.li: Open the gate. We're not afraid.

gloomy.li: Shut away, we'll wither. Open the gates while there's anyone left out there.

plain.li: An open gate is an open invitation, and not everyone who accepts is friendly.
I want to know who's inside the walls. With the gate open, I won't.

warm.li: I like visitors. I'd just like to know them before they're at our table.

cheerful.li: Open gates? Lock up the good spoons, then.

cold.li: Every visitor is a pair of eyes counting our defenses.
